items.front: In Amazon ECS, task role or task execution role: which one does the application code use to call Amazon S3?
items.extra: The execution role [grants the Amazon ECS container and Fargate agents](../facts/ecs.md#ecs-task-execution-role-for-agents) permissions, and they [aren't directly accessible by the containers](../facts/ecs.md#ecs-task-execution-role-for-agents).

items.front: In AWS Fargate, can a task run a privileged container, for example Docker in Docker?
items.extra: On Fargate, [privileged containers or access are currently unavailable](../facts/fargate.md#fargate-no-privileged-containers).

items.front: A company runs Kubernetes in a data center with no connection to AWS. Which Amazon EKS option runs the clusters?
items.extra: EKS Hybrid Nodes keep the control plane in AWS, so they [must have a reliable connection](../facts/eks.md#eks-hybrid-nodes-need-reliable-connection) to AWS.

items.front: In an ECS service on Fargate, can the load balancer target group use the instance target type?
items.back: No. Use the ip target type.
items.extra: The tasks are [associated with an elastic network interface](../facts/fargate.md#fargate-target-group-ip-target-type), not with an EC2 instance.

items.front: In an Amazon ECS service, the team must test a new version before it gets production traffic. Which deployment type fits?
items.extra: It runs [two identical production environments called blue and green](../facts/ecs.md#ecs-blue-green-definition-and-zero-downtime). A rolling update replaces the running tasks instead.

items.front: In Amazon ECS, service auto scaling or cluster auto scaling: which one adds EC2 instances to the cluster?
items.extra: It lets Amazon ECS [manage the scaling of Amazon EC2 instances](../facts/ecs.md#ecs-cluster-auto-scaling-managed-scaling-asg-capacity-provider). Service auto scaling changes the desired number of tasks.

items.front: In Amazon ECR, can tasks in every Region pull from one repository with no extra latency or cost?
items.back: No. ECR is a Regional service.
items.extra: A pull from another Region has [additional latency and data transfer costs](../facts/ecr.md#ecr-faq-cross-region-pull-latency-and-transfer-cost). Replicate the images instead.

items.front: In AWS Lambda, one invocation of a function can run for {{c1::15 minutes per invocation}}; a Fargate task has no such limit.
In Fargate Spot, before AWS takes the capacity back, a task gets a {{c1::two-minute warning}}.
In Fargate Spot, interruption-tolerant ECS tasks run at {{c1::up to a 70 percent discount}} off the Fargate price.
In AWS Fargate, a Linux task is billed {{c1::per second with a 1-minute minimum}}.
In AWS Fargate, an ECS task gets {{c1::20 GiB}} of ephemeral storage by default.
